figures.caption: Figure 4: Real-world OOD settings for Pick Strawberries under four conditions: V1, standard; V2, novel backgrounds; V3, altered lighting; and V4, unseen distractor objects. Bars from top to bottom show the success rates (%) of Joint-WAM, Fast-WAM, and Faster-WAM, respectively.

Figure 3: Real-world success rates on four tasks: T1, Pick Strawberries; T2, Build Tower; T3, Store Boxes; and T4, Stack Plates. Bars from top to bottom show the success rates (%) of Joint-WAM, Fast-WAM, and Faster-WAM, respectively.

Table 5: Success rates (%) on LIBERO-Plus across seven distribution shifts. (a) Future conditioning ablation comparing FasterWAM with its current-only (C-O) counterpart and Fast-WAM. (b) Cumulative component ablation progressively removing Interval KV-Fusion, SparseMoT, and one-pass reusable future context. (c) Interaction-stride ablation comparing dense interaction with increasingly sparse video–action interaction.

Figure 2: Overview of Faster-WAM. (a) Overall framework of Faster-WAM, featuring SparseMoT for selective video–action interaction and Interval KV-Fusion for aggregating multi-level future representations. (b) Inference comparison between JointWAM and Faster-WAM, contrasting iterative dense coupling with one-pass future-context caching and sparse interaction.
Table 3: Success rates (%) on LIBERO-Plus across seven distribution shifts. P.T. denotes embodied pretraining. The best and second-best average results are shown in bold and underlined, respectively.
